content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text resolves the Acts 2:30 collision by noting that the text does not name whose body is the channel, so it is doing the chain-vs-chain evaluation governed by K-C.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "D5 vs C1 (Acts 2:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- the defender answered the loins/bowels rows with the depth idiom (Genesis 46:26; Hebrews 7:9-10) in [CR3] LINK 5 premise 1, and the challenger answered Matthew 1:16 and Galatians 4:4 in [DR3] C1; the text names the seed of David 'according to the flesh' without naming whose body is the channel, so the point stays open.", "rule_words": "When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.", "room": "weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse: read one, the judge must compare the whole chains' support and cannot leave a point open merely because no single verse names the channel; read two, the judge may decide underdetermined by noting that the verse does not name the channel without a full footing comparison.", "why": "The judge text leaves the point open because the pressed text does not name whose body is the channel, which is the retired stating-verse/word-level test rather than a chain-against-chain weighing by footing."}
